BENECON312.name: Econometrics

Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

options.label: Security, Conflict and Governance
options.concept: Study political institutions, conflict, public law and the history of warfare. Explore responses to violent extremism and use qualitative methods, data analysis and economics to investigate questions about conflict and governance.

options.label: Disaster Risk and Societal Resilience
options.concept: Study how natural hazards, climate change and disease outbreaks affect communities. Use psychology, sociology and public policy to examine vulnerability and collective responses. Begin with a team inquiry into a regional sustainability problem, then develop skills in behavioural statistics and qualitative research.

options.label: Digital Systems and Security Governance
options.concept: Study how networks, operating systems and databases work. Combine programming, data analysis and AI ethics with international relations, public law and European governance to examine the policy questions raised by digital systems.

analysis: The closest response combines political institutions, international relations, the history of warfare, Peace & Conflict, Youth Resilience to Extremism, public law and complementary economic and empirical methods. The disaster option substitutes geoscience, epidemiology, climate, behavioural and social science, sustainability governance and a partner research project; the project can run only in term one and has no prerequisite. Later study develops methods the project introduces. Leiden’s second project follows the first project and produces practitioner-facing security policy advice. The digital option responds to the verified minor through programming, networks, database authorisation, algorithms and AI ethics, reinforced by international law and EU governance. Networks & Operating Systems covers internet architecture and protocols directly and displaced Business & Economy in the Age of AI. The option provides technical literacy and governance context; it does not claim training in security operations or direct equivalents for the full minor. The three separately qualified directions exhaust the evidence-backed option limit.

alignment.rationale: Both examine the causes of conflict and approaches to peacebuilding through multiple disciplines.
Both consider violent extremism and responses to it. UCR focuses on protective factors and prevention among young people.
Leiden introduces security and safety as a field across several disciplines.
Leiden uses Syria as a sustained case study in conflict and security.
Leiden examines how societies identify and protect vital assets, interests and values.
Both examine international law in relation to state responses and the use of force. Leiden also considers legal responses to terrorism, cyberattacks and cross-border crime.
Leiden applies economic reasoning directly to safety and security, including issues such as sanctions.
Both investigate disaster risks and responses. Leiden centres on the Fukushima accident, while UCR studies how geoscience can inform risk reduction across hazards.
Both teach statistical analysis for empirical questions. UCR emphasises experimental design and behavioural data, while Leiden includes survey research.
Both involve team inquiry into a problem supplied by an external organisation. Leiden develops security policy advice, while UCR investigates a regional sustainability question.
Both examine how institutions and networks govern collective problems. UCR applies this lens to sustainability.
Both cover technical foundations of networked systems. Leiden also examines threats and responses from policy and societal perspectives.
Both develop academic work and communication skills. Leiden teaches and assesses those skills within Security Studies.
Both introduce research design and the use of evidence. UCR includes descriptive and inferential statistics.
Both develop qualitative research design, interviewing and interpretation. Leiden applies these methods within Security Studies.
Leiden develops research, data interpretation and debating skills in its second lab.
Leiden integrates safety analysis, teamwork and communication in its third lab.
Leiden requires a team project on gender-based violence.
Leiden requires a 15 EC individual Security Studies thesis.
Leiden reserves 30 EC for student-selected study.
